clue.text: Man flies off — only to be shot down…

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man takes off in an aircraft, only to be brought down by enemy fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals rearranging MANFLIES; the trailing dots let 'shot down' describe the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft shot down typically goes down burning, ablaze with fire.

clue.text: The head wants a bit of pasta

definitions.meaning: slang for the head or brain

explanation.surface: Someone's head is craving a little pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal slang for the head or brain, and also a strip of pasta.

clue.text: Allowed to run!

definitions.meaning: British slang for running away fast, as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for lawful, and 'leg it' is British slang meaning flee on foot.

clue.text: Half-way through the main dish

parts.note: reads like being partway through eating a dinner's principal plate, but also means at the midpoint of any journey or course

explanation.surface: A diner is part-way through eating the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: The main dish of a meal comes in the middle of the courses, which gives the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Midcourse means at the midpoint of a route or process, and the main dish is the middle serving of a meal.

clue.text: Resolved to give subsidy, despite hitch

parts.note: resolved, as in set on doing something, gives set
to back a project is to fund or support it

explanation.surface: Someone was determined to fund a project in spite of a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or reverse, something that delays progress.

clue.text: Happen to live with constraint, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is said aloud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: to live with constraint is to be tied, two words

explanation.surface: Someone happens to have to live under restrictions, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Betide is an old verb meaning occur or befall, as in 'woe betide'.

clue.text: Type of band that makes money

definitions.meaning: a band of trumpets, tubas and cornets

explanation.surface: A kind of band that earns a lot of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band plays metal wind instruments, and brass is northern British slang for cash.

clue.text: A sign he's included for word-lovers

indicators.note: included means the letters of he's are placed inside the zodiac sign

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign that includes him is just the thing for lovers of words.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a book made for word-lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book of synonyms is a natural companion for people who love vocabulary.

clue.text: I'd been upset by tough urban area

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters of I'd are turned over, read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
tough, as in a tough rule, means strict

explanation.surface: Someone was distressed by a hard part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a defined part of a town or city, a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Determined to be kept track of

definitions.meaning: followed closely, as a hound follows a trail

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved to be followed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged means stubbornly persistent, and to be dogged is to be followed or shadowed.

clue.text: Go over to view retro paintings and poetry

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the word for paintings is read in reverse

parts.note: paintings are art
poetry is verse

explanation.surface: Cross over to see some old-fashioned pictures and poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns ART into TRA; 'to view' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross or travel across something.

clue.text: Patrol he reorganised to excess

indicators.note: reorganised means the letters of the patrol and he are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man reorganised the patrol to an excessive degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, far more than enough.

clue.text: Glittering display of VIPs

definitions.meaning: twinkling, shining like the night sky

explanation.surface: A sparkling showing of very important people.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry means sparkling with lights, and a starry event is packed with celebrities.

clue.text: Their trick is contrived to make money fast

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people's cunning scheme is designed to get quick profits.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike it rich is an idiom for suddenly becoming wealthy.

clue.text: Underwriter has to make a donation

parts.note: sub is a Latin prefix meaning under
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: An insurance underwriter is obliged to give money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwriter' is split into UNDER and WRITER.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe is to pledge or contribute money to a cause.

clue.text: Reporter sees popular chap in garrison

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in means the word for chap goes inside the word for garrison

parts.note: a fort is a garrisoned stronghold
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A journalist meets a well-liked fellow in a military post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporter' suggests a journalist, but here it is someone who informs on others; 'sees' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An informant reports information to authorities, often secretly.

clue.text: Study treatise to gain agreement

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: Reading a learned paper in order to win consensus.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding agreement between parties.

clue.text: They somehow bamboozle two banks

parts.note: double means twofold
bluffs are steep banks or cliffs

explanation.surface: Some people trick a couple of financial institutions.
explanation.definitionFit: A double bluff is a ruse in which the truth is told expecting it to be disbelieved, deceiving the listener.

clue.text: Many a male with talent is radiant

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, standing for many
a bent is a natural talent

explanation.surface: Many a gifted man shines brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a soft, flickering glow, as of light playing on a surface.

clue.text: Whack fellow for taking bandage

parts.note: to swat is to strike or whack
he stands for a fellow, a male person

explanation.surface: Someone hits a man for removing a dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is a strip of cloth used to wrap or bind, like a dressing.

clue.text: Eleven chimneys

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Eleven chimneys' (6): 'chimneys' defines STACKS but 'Eleven' gives no sense or letters for it; the clue seems garbled and a search found no other text.

clue.text: Change into a loose dress

explanation.surface: Get changed into a baggy frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift is to move or alter, and a shift is a simple straight-cut dress.

clue.text: Retail reduction must be put in writing

definitions.meaning: a cut in a shop's price

explanation.surface: A shop's price cut has to be recorded on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A markdown is a lowered selling price, and to mark down is to write something down.

clue.text: Tennis player's lost the advantage, darn it!

definitions.meaning: the score returns to forty-all when the player with advantage loses the next point

explanation.surface: A frustrated tennis player curses after losing the advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuce is the tied tennis score reached again after an advantage is lost, and an old euphemism for the devil used as an oath.

clue.text: Woman embraces man by the sea

indicators.note: embraces means the woman's name wraps around the man's name

parts.note: Marie is a woman's name
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A woman hugs a man at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' is the container signal: the woman's name wraps around the man's.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to or bordering on the ocean.

clue.text: A union leader in Leeds, say, displays sharpness

indicators.note: in means the union leader goes inside the word for Leeds

parts.note: Leeds is an example of a city in northern England

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of union

explanation.surface: A trade union leader in Leeds shows keen intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives U and 'in' puts it inside CITY; 'say' marks Leeds as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is keenness of mind or perception.

clue.text: Confirm that attorney is in Lille

parts.note: Att is an abbreviation for attorney
est is French for is, as spoken in the French city of Lille

explanation.surface: Verify that a lawyer is in the French city of Lille.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare or bear witness that something is true.

clue.text: Treat Ted badly for looking down at heel

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of treat and Ted are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone treats Ted poorly because he looks shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals rearranging TREATTED. 'Down at heel' means shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are ragged and torn give a shabby, down-at-heel appearance.
